connection_condition: atom.molecule_id identifies the molecule that owns each atom row; an atom row cannot be interpreted without its molecule.
description: A molecule is composed of its atoms; the atom table is the part-of decomposition of the molecule into atomic sites.

connection_condition: bond.molecule_id identifies the molecule that owns each bond row; bond rows are recorded per molecule.
description: A molecule is composed of its bonds; the bond table is the part-of decomposition of the molecule into chemical bonds.
A hydrogen atom is a specific kind of atom: the 5518 rows with element 'h' form a subset of the 12333 atom rows.
A heavy atom is a specific kind of atom: the 6815 rows whose element is not 'h' form a subset of the 12333 atom rows and are disjoint from hydrogen atoms.

connection_condition: atom.element carries the element symbol inline; there is no element table and no element identifier to join through.
description: Every atom realises exactly one chemical element, but element identity is stored as an inline symbol on the atom row rather than as a referenced dimension record.

connection_condition: bond.bond_type carries the bond-order symbol inline on each bond row; no bond-type table or code column exists.
description: The bond-type category classifies every bond, but the classification is stored as an inline symbol on the bond rather than as a referenced category record.

connection_condition: connected.bond_id references bond.bond_id, and connected.atom_id / connected.atom_id2 are the two atoms of that bond; each bond_id appears exactly twice in connected.
description: Each bond is decomposed into exactly two directed adjacency entries, one per direction; a connectivity entry has no meaning without the bond it came from.
Atom degree is derived from the connectivity relation by counting the distinct bonded neighbours of each atom; no degree column exists in the database.
Molecule atom count is derived by counting atom rows per molecule; it is not stored as a column.
Molecule bond count is derived by counting bond rows per molecule; it must be derived from the bond table, since counting connectivity entries would double the value.
